subject: QBR infra sprint: capacity runway snapshot & immediate asks
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR infra sprint: capacity runway snapshot & immediate asks

Team — quick heads-up ahead of QBR prep sprint (T-12 days). I pulled a compact runway snapshot and a short set of asks that will need leadership-level sign-off before we finalize the QBR deck. Attachment: runway_snapshot_v2.xlsx; batching-sim-aug7.csv.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Committed GPU pool (prod + reserved): 1.2k A100-equivalent slots; baseline utilization: 62% last 30d (tokens/slot).
- Forecast for Q4 uplift (feature launches + PLG spike): median demand +28%, 90th percentile +55%.
- Unit economics drivers: batching window, KV-prefix cache hit, and quantization plan. Current per-1k-token cost estimate: $0.93; with expected optimizations we can hit $0.72-$0.78.
- Risk: sustained P95 latency degradation when batching window > 12ms for RPCs that are latency-sensitive; this surfaces for ~18% of traffic (chat interactive).

Leadership asks (decision items for next 48h):
1) Approve a 2-week burst budget to buy 150 A100-equivalent hours from SpotCloud for on-demand capacity to cover the Q4 headroom while we finalize Dedicated scaling. Estimated incremental spend: $46k.
2) Approve a canary to reduce prefix-KV TTL from 300s -> 90s for chat-only shards to validate cache-hit delta and correctness. If hit rate drops <8%, abort.
3) Greenlight a prioritized quantization experiment (int8 on 1: top-line models) to be run in the infra sprint; we need Prod-sim results to include in QBR (risk: minor quality delta to eval).
4) Permit infra to re-route non-interactive batch traffic to cheaper regions (eu/apac) during the weekend burst window; requires legal sign-off for any data locality exceptions.

What I need from you now: 
- Lauren: a one-line preference on the burst budget (approve / request further analysis) so I can lock SpotCloud pricing.
- Irene: can infra land the cache TTL canary in 24h? If not, propose alternate timing.
- Marissa: devrel/ops needs a short note for customer-facing comms in case we start regional reroutes (Nimbus Apps referenced).

I kept the attached workbook minimal — first tab is a spend sensitivity by batching window; second tab is utilization scenarios. I'll update with the canary SOP after we decide.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Dylan / Lauren — I can run the TTL canary in 24-36h but a few implementation notes:

- Canary scope: chat-only shards (production tag: chat_v2_*), 5% of chat traffic. That limits customer exposure and gives sample size for cache-hit measurement.
- Expected cache behavior: our simulation (attached) shows a ~18% reduction in per-token inference time with the current TTL at baseline; reducing TTL to 90s reduces hit by ~6-9% on chat flows but reduces stale-state risk for short-lived contexts. Net token cost reduction estimate: -12% when combined with batching optimizations.
- Batching note: increasing batching window from 8ms -> 20ms yields 14% uplift in throughput but P95 latency increases ~210ms for interactive calls. Suggest we cap the interactive path at 12ms and route tolerant bulk calls to windows up to 40ms.
- Quantization: safe to run int8 on the internal stg cluster; we need an eval pass against the hard prompt set (500 prompts) to detect regressions. Time estimate: 48h to run and 12h to analyze.

I'll push cache_sim_notes.pdf to the QBR folder and trigger the canary once I get Lauren's sign-off and confirmation that legal OKs the weekend reroute for data locality.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Following up after a quick sim on the batch windows and a short legal check re: regional reroutes. Attaching quick-sim-results-aug9.csv. Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/QBR-2028/infra-runway (dylan's folder), HubSpot:HS-000241 (tracking ticket for Nimbus comms).

Findings: 
- Short weekend reroute to eu for 12 hours (non-personal telemetry only) reduces projected spend by ~9.6% on the burst and keeps interactive P95 within SLA for US customers. Legal signed off on a limited exception scoped to telemetry and non-PII payloads; full customer-facing data must still remain in-region.
- Quick sim aligns with Irene's note: cap interactive batching at 12ms, route embeddings/batch jobs to 40ms windows.
- SpotCloud: I got a hold on pricing; I recommend we lock the 150 A100-eq hours purchase contingent on finance sign-off. If approved, ops will provision a conservative rolling allocation during the burst.

I'll draft the Nimbus comms tonight and share the one-pager Lauren asked for by EOD Monday (two slides: econ sensitivity + ops playbook).

-Marissa
